steps.title: O₂ plasma etch slides
steps.instruction: Place 25 mm × 75 mm glass slides in a plasma etcher, run O₂ plasma at 300 mbar and 100 W for 10 min; measure water contact angle before and after treatment.

steps.title: Prepare anhydrous toluene
steps.instruction: Add 4 Å molecular sieves to toluene to obtain a 20 % w/v suspension and store for 24 h to dry the solvent.

steps.title: Silanise slides with GPTMS
steps.instruction: Immediately after plasma, submerge slides in 500 mL anhydrous toluene (crystallisation dish) on a hot plate set to 50 °C under argon; add 10 mL GPTMS and stir for 24 h; cool to room temperature, wash slides three times with fresh acetone, dry under vacuum <50 mTorr for 24 h; confirm silanisation by water contact angle (≈54 ° ± 1.1 °).

steps.title: Prepare 4 % pHEMA solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve pHEMA to 4 % w/v in ethanol (95 % v/v ethanol in deionised distilled water); optionally sonicate 2 g pHEMA in 50 mL solvent for 24 h; keep solution sealed to avoid evaporation and prepare fresh for each coating session.

steps.title: Dip‑coat slides with pHEMA
steps.instruction: Set dip‑coater to 9 mm/s speed, 2 s dip duration, 1 s retention; clip each silanised slide, immerse in 4 % pHEMA solution (in a 100 mL beaker); repeat coating four times, allowing drying between dips; cover beaker to prevent evaporation; after final coat, store slides at ambient conditions for 3 days; evaluate coating uniformity by optical profilometry.

steps.title: Degas monomers under argon
steps.instruction: In a scintillation glass vial add the required monomer, seal with a rubber stopper, wrap cap with parafilm, insert a 21 G 40 mm needle for venting and a 21 G 120 mm needle connected to argon; bubble argon through the monomer for 30 min while the vent needle remains out of the liquid.

steps.title: Prepare DMPA solution
steps.instruction: Weigh DMPA and dissolve to 2 % w/v in DMF in a polypropylene or glass vial.

steps.title: Form polymerisation solution
steps.instruction: In a glove box (O₂ < 2000 ppm) mix monomer (50 % v/v for liquids or w/v for solids) with DMF and add 1 % DMPA; keep the mixture under argon.

steps.title: Load polymer solutions onto plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 40 µL of each polymerisation solution into wells of a 384‑well polypropylene source plate and place the plate on the microarray printer stage.

steps.title: Set printer environment
steps.instruction: Adjust printer chamber to O₂ < 2000 ppm and humidity 30–40 %; wash pins with isopropanol, install the 16‑pin print head, close the chamber, launch BioDot AxSys software and recalibrate X, Y, Z axes.

steps.title: Pre‑spot plasma‑etched slide
steps.instruction: Perform four pre‑spots on a plasma‑etched (non‑pHEMA) glass slide to condition the pins.

steps.title: Print polymer spots on pHEMA slide
steps.instruction: Align the pHEMA‑coated slide, print spots (e.g., 56 spots over a 7 mm × 7 mm area with 850 µm spacing and alternating ±850 µm offset); use two contacts per position to blot excess; after each spot, cure with 365 nm UV for 40 s; wash the pin in DMF and dry three times before the next spot.

steps.title: Post‑print UV cure and vacuum
steps.instruction: After all spots are printed, expose the slide to an additional 20 min UV; place the slide in vacuum <50 mTorr for 24 h; optionally perform a second print offset by 800 µm for full coverage and repeat the printing step; finally keep the slide in <50 mTorr vacuum for at least 7 days to remove residual solvent and unpolymerised monomer.

steps.title: Clean ProPlate chambers
steps.instruction: Make a washing solution of 0.1 % v/v Tween 20 in PBS; soak chambers and snap clips for 15 min; rinse three times with deionised water; soak overnight in isopropanol; air‑dry before use.

steps.title: Assess chamber leakage
steps.instruction: Add trypan blue dye to alternating wells of the assembled chambers and incubate for 7 days (or the experimental duration); verify that dye does not migrate between wells.

steps.title: Assemble chambers on printed slide
steps.instruction: Place the 16‑well ProPlate superstructure onto the polymer‑printed slide and secure with snap clips as illustrated.

steps.title: Verify polymer by ATR‑FTIR
steps.instruction: Scan each printed area with ATR‑FTIR (254 scans, 600–4000 cm⁻¹, 4 cm⁻¹ resolution) and subtract air background after each scan to confirm polymer formation.

steps.title: Perform cell viability assay
steps.instruction: Seed primary cells (moDCs or MDMs) onto polymer spots, incubate 24 h, collect supernatant and measure adenylate kinase release using the ToxiLight assay according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Collect secretome for ELISA
steps.instruction: After 24 h culture, collect supernatants and assay TNF‑α, IL‑10, TGF‑β1, CCL‑18, IL‑6 and IL‑12 using high‑binding 384‑well plates and ELISA DuoSet kits, following the kit instructions.

description: Validation of protocol Presence of polymers (fabricated using this platform) on the surface of the substrate was validated by ATR-FTIR. The applicability of this platform for cell culture was validated by culturing two different primary cell types and assessing cell viability and cytokine secretion: Chemical characterisation: ATR-FTIR spectra was used to validate the presence of specific chemical components or functional groups on the substrate surface following contact printing and in situ UV polymerisation. Spectra were obtained by scanning the samples (254 scans) from 600 to 4,000 cm -1 with a 4 cm -1 resolution, with subtraction against background (air) after each scan. The analysis of the printed polymers' spectra reveals significant distinctions when compared to pHEMA. Specifically, the O–H stretching (3,550–3,200 cm -1 ) present in the pHEMA spectra is no longer evident, and distinct new peaks have emerged in the polymer spectrum in the fingerprint region (400–1,500 cm -1 ). For example, the ATR-FTIR analysis clearly confirms the conversion of ethoxyethyl acrylate (EOEA) monomer into a polymer (pEOEA). The disappearance of the C=C stretching peak at 1,640 cm -1 , characteristic of the monomer, in the polymer spectrum, along with the presence of typical acrylate polymer peaks (e.g., C=O stretching at 1,720 cm -1 ), indicates successful polymerisation as shown in Figure 7A and B. Figure 7. Attenuated total reflectance–Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) spectra of pHEMA and ethoxy ethyl acrylate (EOEA) monomer (red) and its corresponding printed polymer (blue). A. The spectra of pHEMA shows O–H stretching (3,550–3,200 cm -1 ), C–H stretching, corresponding aliphatic stretching vibration of CH 2 (3,000–2,840 cm -1 ), and C=O stretching (1725 cm -1 ). B.
